tagline: Over the Markagunt Plateau, on a road once walked on quilts.
intro: Out of Parowan, SR-143 turns up the canyon past the red Vermilion Cliffs and the White Cliffs, then makes the steep pull to Brian Head, Utah's highest town. Past the ski town it climbs over 10,000 feet at the edge of Cedar Breaks, turns east, and comes down through aspen and old lava fields to Panguitch Lake and along Panguitch Creek into Panguitch.

The name goes back to the winter of 1864. Frost had killed most of the new settlers' crops at Panguitch, and seven men set out over the mountain for flour from Parowan. When snow stopped the wagons they went on foot, laying one quilt after another on the snow, the story goes, to keep from sinking.

moments.title: Cedar Breaks National Monument
moments.text: From the North View the amphitheater falls away more than 2,000 feet, three miles of eroded rock, and bristlecone pines more than 1,600 years old grow in the high country.

moments.title: Panguitch Lake
moments.text: A natural lake raised by a 24-foot dam, fished first by the Paiute. Panguitch is their word for big fish.

moments.title: Panguitch
moments.text: The settlers fired local clay into rose-colored brick and paid their workers in it. The workers built their own houses with their wages, and those rose brick houses still stand.

practical: Between Parowan and Brian Head the grade reaches 13 percent and is not recommended for RVs or semi-trucks. The stretch from Brian Head to Panguitch may close in bad winter weather.
